full_judgment: 3.3 Among others, these petitioners as defendants Nos.5-7 and 12-17 entered appearance and contested the suit by way of submitting a joint written statement denying materials allegations made in the plaint and contended therein, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable with the simple prayer for partition and that the suit suffers from defect of parties and hotchpot. It is further contended that long before the suit the disputed properties were partitioned amicably by mets and bounds between the predecessors of the parties by a deed of partition dated 30-6-1939. Shaheb Ullah Pramanik, Mohit Ullah Pramanik and Mohorbi Bewa transferred two- wan (a local land measurement in Bogra) of land out of the suit land in favour of Shahebullah Pramanik, the predecessor of these defendants-appellants-petitioners vide registered sale deed dated 10-2-1925. The said land of two wans measuring 58 decimals were recorded in plot No. 3124 and 4735 in CS Khatian No.889 but CS Khatian No.1477 was erroneously written in the said sale deed out of bonafide mistake. After the said sale deed was registered, Syeedullah Pramanik, Mohitullah Pramanik and Shaharbi Bewa got their title extinguished to the said amount of land. It is further stated that Syed Ali Pramanik, the predecessor of the plaintiffs-respondents-opposite parties, was the party to the said partition deed dated 30-6-1939 and in view of thereof MRR Khatian was prepared in the name of the parties to the partition deed. As per partition deed, Syed Ali Pramanik acquired 1.28 acres of land in CS Khatian No.1388 (schedule 2 to the plaint) and 1.06 acres of land in CS Khatian No.218 (schedule No.1) totaling 2.34 acres of land and MRR Khatian Nos. 237 and 442 were correctly prepared in his name. After the demise of Syed Ali Pramanik, the plaintiffs-respondents-opposite parties inherited 2.34 acres of land in the partible holdings and that they have no right, title and interest in any land in CS khatian no 889 (Schedule 3). They are only entitled to 2.34 acres of land. In the above circumstances, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
